title: Scheduled Maintenance Window Validator
description: Build a complete maintenance scheduling system: validate operations occur within maintenance windows, track durations, calculate next scheduled events.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Ship maintenance must happen during designated windows—00:00-06:00 daily. Build a validator that checks if operations occur during valid windows, calculates duration, and schedules next maintenance."
story.context: Production systems have maintenance windows. This challenge tests complete DateTime mastery: time windows, duration validation, scheduling, and time-based decision logic.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Outstanding! You validated 5 operations, identified window violations, calculated durations, and scheduled next maintenance. This is production-grade time management!"

instructions: Create *** Settings *** with Library    DateTime and Library    Collections
- Operation 2: name=Backup, start=2025-10-04 05:00:00, duration=2 hours (INVALID - exceeds window)
- Operation 4: name=Update, start=2025-10-04 08:00:00, duration=1 hour (INVALID - outside window)
- Operation 5: name=Scan, start=2025-10-04 04:00:00, duration=1 hour 30 minutes (valid)
- FOR each valid operation from previous test:
- Log    Next maintenance window in ${hours} hours
hints: Use Get Substring to extract hour from timestamp
Add Time To Date to calculate operation end time
Compare hour >= 0 and hour < 6 for window validation
Parse duration strings: '1 hour', '30 minutes', '1 hour 30 minutes'
For next midnight: Add Time To Date with calculated hours
solution:
*** Settings ***
Library    DateTime
Library    Collections

*** Test Cases ***
Validate Maintenance Operations
    @{operations}=    Create List
    &{op1}=    Create Dictionary    name=Diagnostic    start=2025-10-04 02:30:00    duration=1 hour
    &{op2}=    Create Dictionary    name=Backup    start=2025-10-04 05:00:00    duration=2 hours
    &{op3}=    Create Dictionary    name=Cleanup    start=2025-10-04 01:00:00    duration=30 minutes
    &{op4}=    Create Dictionary    name=Update    start=2025-10-04 08:00:00    duration=1 hour
    &{op5}=    Create Dictionary    name=Scan    start=2025-10-04 04:00:00    duration=1 hour 30 minutes
    Append To List    ${operations}    ${op1}    ${op2}    ${op3}    ${op4}    ${op5}
    
    ${valid_count}=    Set Variable    0
    ${invalid_count}=    Set Variable    0
    @{valid_ops}=    Create List
    
    FOR    ${op}    IN    @{operations}
        ${name}=    Get From Dictionary    ${op}    name
        ${start}=    Get From Dictionary    ${op}    start
        ${duration}=    Get From Dictionary    ${op}    duration
        
        ${end_time}=    Add Time To Date    ${start}    ${duration}
        ${start_hour}=    Get Substring    ${start}    11    13
        ${end_hour}=    Get Substring    ${end_time}    11    13
        ${start_hour_num}=    Convert To Integer    ${start_hour}
        ${end_hour_num}=    Convert To Integer    ${end_hour}
        
        ${valid}=    Set Variable    False
        IF    ${start_hour_num} >= 0 and ${start_hour_num} < 6
            IF    ${end_hour_num} <= 6 or ${end_hour_num} == 0
                ${valid}=    Set Variable    True
                ${valid_count}=    Set Variable    ${valid_count + 1}
                Append To List    ${valid_ops}    ${op}
                Log    ${name}: VALID (${start} to ${end_time})
            ELSE
                ${invalid_count}=    Set Variable    ${invalid_count + 1}
                Log    ${name}: INVALID (ends after 06:00)
            END
        ELSE
            ${invalid_count}=    Set Variable    ${invalid_count + 1}
            Log    ${name}: INVALID (starts outside window)
        END
    END
    
    Log    Valid: ${valid_count}, Invalid: ${invalid_count}
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${valid_count}    3
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${invalid_count}    2
    Set Suite Variable    @{VALID_OPS}    @{valid_ops}

Calculate Total Maintenance Time
    ${total_seconds}=    Set Variable    0
    FOR    ${op}    IN    @{VALID_OPS}
        ${duration}=    Get From Dictionary    ${op}    duration
        # Convert duration to seconds (simplified - assumes hours/minutes format)
        ${hours}=    Set Variable    0
        ${minutes}=    Set Variable    0
        IF    'hour' in '${duration}'
            IF    '1 hour 30' in '${duration}'
                ${hours}=    Set Variable    1
                ${minutes}=    Set Variable    30
            ELSE IF    '1 hour' in '${duration}'
                ${hours}=    Set Variable    1
            ELSE IF    '2 hour' in '${duration}'
                ${hours}=    Set Variable    2
            END
        END
        IF    '30 minutes' in '${duration}' and 'hour' not in '${duration}'
            ${minutes}=    Set Variable    30
        END
        ${seconds}=    Evaluate    (${hours} * 3600) + (${minutes} * 60)
        ${total_seconds}=    Set Variable    ${total_seconds + ${seconds}}
    END
    ${total_hours}=    Evaluate    ${total_seconds} / 3600
    Log    Total maintenance time: ${total_hours} hours
    Should Be True    ${total_hours} >= 3

Schedule Next Maintenance
    ${now}=    Get Current Date    result_format=%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S
    ${tomorrow}=    Add Time To Date    ${now}    1 day
    ${next_window}=    Convert Date    ${tomorrow}    result_format=%Y-%m-%d
    ${next_window}=    Set Variable    ${next_window} 00:00:00
    ${hours_until}=    Subtract Date From Date    ${next_window}    ${now}
    ${hours}=    Evaluate    ${hours_until} / 3600
    Log    Next maintenance window: ${next_window}
    Log    Hours until next window: ${hours}
    Should Not Be Empty    ${next_window}

theory.title: Challenge 4.3: Maintenance Window Validator
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "This is real-world operations, PROTO-7. Production systems have maintenance windows. Violate them and you impact users. This challenge tests everything: time parsing, arithmetic, validation, scheduling—complete time management."

Complete Time Management Workflow

Production maintenance requires:

  • Window validation: Is operation within allowed hours?
  • Duration calculation: Will operation complete in time?
  • Time arithmetic: Add duration to start time
  • Comparison logic: Hour extraction and numeric comparison
  • Aggregation: Total maintenance time
  • Scheduling: Calculate next window

⚠️ Challenge Architecture

  • Input: 5 operation dicts (name, start, duration)
  • Validation: Check start hour 0-6, end time <= 06:00
  • Time extraction: Get Substring for hour parsing
  • Arithmetic: Add Time To Date for end calculation
  • Filtering: FOR + IF to find valid operations
  • Aggregation: Sum durations of valid operations
  • Scheduling: Calculate next midnight timestamp
  • Expected: 3 valid, 2 invalid operations

Real-World Applications

This challenge demonstrates patterns used in:

  • Maintenance window enforcement
  • Backup scheduling and validation
  • Deployment window management
  • SLA compliance checking
  • Resource scheduling systems

You've mastered DateTime library—essential for all time-based automation.
